label: lem:convex
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:convex}
    If $\gamma$ is sufficiently large, then on $\mathcal{Q}$, the map $\mathfrak F_\gamma:(\mathbf{p},\mathbf{Q}) \mapsto \Psi_\gamma(W_{\mathbf{p},\mathbf{Q}})$ is convex.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider any $(\mathbf p,\mathbf Q)\in \mathcal Q$, any $\mathbf u=(u_1,\dots,u_k)\in \mathbb R^k$ with $u_1+\dots+u_k=0$, and any vector $\mathbf V=(V_{ij})_{i,j=1}^k$ of functions $V_{ij}:[0,1]^2\to \mathbb R$ such that $V_{ij}(x,y)=V_{ji}(y,x)$ for each $i,j,x,y$. Our objective is to show that the second variation of $\mathfrak F_\gamma$ at $(\mathbf p,\mathbf Q)$ with respect to the perturbation $(\mathbf u,\mathbf V)$ is nonnegative. That is to say, we want to show that the map
    $F_\gamma:\delta\mapsto \mathfrak F_\gamma(\mathbf p+\delta\mathbf u,\mathbf Q+\delta\mathbf V)$
    satisfies $F_\gamma''(0)\ge 0$. This is a fairly routine matter of estimating the relevant Hessian, but the calculations are a little involved.

    First, we write \[\mathfrak F_\gamma(\mathbf p,\mathbf Q)=\mathfrak G(\mathbf p,\mathbf Q)+\gamma \mathfrak T(\mathbf p,\mathbf Q),\qquad G(\delta)=\mathfrak G(\mathbf p+\delta\mathbf u,\mathbf Q+\delta\mathbf V),\qquad T(\delta)=\mathfrak T(\mathbf p+\delta\mathbf u,\mathbf Q+\delta\mathbf V),\] where
    \begin{align*}\mathfrak G(\mathbf p,\mathbf Q)&=\sum_{i,j=1}^kp_ip_j\int g(Q_{ij}),\\\mathfrak T(\mathbf p,\mathbf Q)&=
\sum_{\phi:\operatorname V(H)\to[k]}
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\prod_{a\in V(H)}p_{\phi(a)}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)
\int_{x_1,\dots,x_{v(H)}}
\prod_{ab\in E(H)}
Q_{\phi(a)\phi(b)}(x_a,x_b)\end{align*}
(here we write $[k]=\{1,\dots,k\}$).

\medskip \noindent\textit{Step 1: The entropy term.}
We compute
\[G''(0)= \sum_{i, j} p_ip_j \int \frac{V_{ij}^2}{Q_{ij}} \;\;+ 2\sum_{i, j} u_iu_j \int g(Q_{ij}) \;\;+ 4\sum_{i, j}p_i u_j \int V_{ij} \log Q_{ij}\]
(where all sums are over $i,j\in \{1,\dots,k\}$). Since $(\mathbf{p}, \mathbf{Q}) \in \mathcal{Q}$, we have 
    \[
        \sum_{i, j=1}^k u_iu_j \int g(Q_{ij}) \ge g\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big(e^{-\alpha\gamma})\sum_i u_i^2-g(1-e^{-\alpha \gamma})\sum_{i,j}|u_iu_j|\ge \frac12 \sum_i u_i^2, 
    \]
    and 
    \[
        \sum_{i, j=1}^k p_ip_j \int \frac{V_{ij}^2}{Q_{ij}} \ge \bigg(\frac{1}{k}- \eta\bigg)^2\Bigg(\sum_{i\ne j} \int V_{ij}^2 +  \sum_{i} \int \frac{V_{ii}^2}{Q_{ii}}\Bigg)
        \ge \frac1{2k^2}\sum_{i\ne j} \int V_{ij}^2 +  \frac1{2k^2}\sum_{i} \int \frac{V_{ii}^2}{Q_{ii}}. 
    \]
    Also,
        \begin{align*}
        \Bigg |\sum_{i, j}p_i u_j \int V_{ij} \log Q_{ij} \Bigg|&\le \frac{2}{k} \sum_{i\ne j} |\log(1-e^{-\alpha\gamma})|\,|u_j|\int |V_{ij}| + \frac{2}{k} \sum_i |u_i| \int \Big(|V_{ii}|\, |\log Q_{ii}|\Big)\\
        &\le  \sum_{i\ne j} e^{-\alpha\gamma/2} |u_j| \sqrt{\int |V_{ij}|^2} +  \sum_i |u_i| \sqrt{\int \frac{V_{ii}^2}{Q_{ii}} \int \Big(Q_{ii}\, |\log Q_{ii}|^2\Big)}\\
        &\le  e^{-\alpha\gamma/2}\sum_{i\ne j}  \sqrt{u_j^2\int |V_{ij}|^2} +  e^{-\alpha\gamma/3} \sum_i \sqrt{u_i^2\int \frac{V_{ii}^2}{Q_{ii}}}\\
        &\le e^{-\alpha\gamma/2}\sum_{i\ne j}  \Bigg(u_j^2+\int V_{ij}^2\Bigg)  + e^{-\alpha\gamma/3} \sum_i \Bigg(u_i^2+ \int \frac{V_{ii}^2}{Q_{ii}}\Bigg),
    \end{align*}
    where in the second line we have used the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and in the last line we have used the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality.
    
    Combining the above estimates, and noting that $(1/(2k^2))Q_{ii}^{-1}\ge e^{\alpha \gamma/2}$, we have
    \begin{equation}
        G''(0)\ge \frac13 \sum_i u_i^2+\frac1{3k^2}\sum_{i\ne j}\int V_{ij}^2+ e^{\alpha \gamma/2}\sum_{i} \int V_{ii}^2.\label{eq:G''}
    \end{equation}
    That is to say, $G''(0)$ has quite a large positive value; it remains to show that $\gamma T''(0)$ cannot be so negative as to cancel this out.

\medskip \noindent\textit{Step 2: The $H$-counting term.}
We compute
\[T''(0)=D_{\mathrm{ee}}+2D_{\mathrm{ev}}+D_{\mathrm{vv}}\]
where for each $\sigma\in \{\mathrm{ee},\mathrm{ev},\mathrm{vv}\}$ we have
\[D_\sigma=\sum_{\phi:\operatorname V(H)\to[k]}
\Bigg(\prod_{a\in V(H)}p_{\phi(a)}\Bigg)
\int_{x_1,\dots,x_{v(H)}}
\Bigg(\prod_{ab\in E(H)}
Q_{\phi(a)\phi(b)}(x_a,x_b)\Bigg)d_\sigma(x_1,\dots,x_{v(H)})\]
with
\begin{align*}d_{\mathrm{ee}}(x_1,\dots,x_{v(H)})&=\sum_{\substack{a_1b_1,a_2b_2\in H\\\text{distinct}}} \frac{V_{\phi(a_1)\phi(b_1)}(x_{a_1},x_{b_1})V_{\phi(a_2)\phi(b_2)}(x_{a_2},x_{b_2})}{Q_{\phi(a_1)\phi(b_1)}(x_{a_1},x_{b_1})Q_{\phi(a_2)\phi(b_2)}(x_{a_2},x_{b_2})},\\
d_{\mathrm{ev}}(x_1,\dots,x_{v(H)})&=\sum_{v\in \operatorname V(H),ab\in H} \frac{u_{\phi(v)}V_{\phi(a)\phi(b)}(x_{a},x_{b})}{p_{\phi(v)}Q_{\phi(a)\phi(b)}(x_{a},x_{b})},\\
d_{\mathrm{vv}}(x_1,\dots,x_{v(H)}) &=\sum_{\substack{v_1,v_2\in \operatorname V(H)\\\text{distinct}}} \frac{u_{\phi(v_1)}u_{\phi(v_2)}}{p_{\phi(v_1)}p_{\phi(v_2)}}.
\end{align*}
Since $H$ has chromatic number $k+1$, for every $\phi:\operatorname V(H)\to [k]$ there is an edge $ab\in H$ for which $\phi(a)=\phi(b)$, which implies that $Q_{\phi(a)\phi(b)}\le e^{-\alpha \gamma}$ (recalling the definition of $\mathcal Q$). This will be our main mechanism to bound the various terms in $T''(0)$.

If $\phi(a_1)\ne \phi(b_1)$ and $\phi(a_2)\ne \phi(b_2)$ then the term in $D_{\mathrm{ee}}$ corresponding to $a_1b_1$ and $a_2b_2$ has absolute value at most
\begin{align*}
    &O_{H}\Bigg(e^{-\alpha \gamma}\int_{x_v:v\in\{a_1,b_1,a_2,b_2\}} |V_{\phi(a_1)\phi(b_1)}(x_{a_1},x_{b_1})|\,|V_{\phi(a_2)\phi(b_2)}(x_{a_2},x_{b_2})|\Bigg)\\
    &\qquad \le O_{H}\Bigg(e^{-\alpha \gamma}\sqrt{\int V_{\phi(a_1)\phi(b_1)}^2}\cdot \sqrt{\int V_{\phi(a_2)\phi(b_2)}^2}\Bigg),
\end{align*}
using the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality. If $\phi(a_1)=\phi(b_1)$, the corresponding contribution to $D_{\mathrm{ee}}$ has absolute value at most
\begin{align*}
    &O_{H}\Bigg(\int_{x_v:v\in\{a_1,b_1,a_2,b_2\}} |V_{\phi(a_1)\phi(a_1)}(x_{a_1},x_{b_1})|\,|V_{\phi(a_2)\phi(b_2)}(x_{a_2},x_{b_2})|\Bigg)\\
    &\qquad\le O_{H}\Bigg( \sqrt{e^{\alpha\gamma/4}\int V_{\phi(a_1)\phi(a_1)}^2}\cdot \sqrt{e^{-\alpha\gamma/4}\int V^2_{\phi(a_2)\phi(b_2)}}\Bigg)\\
    &\qquad\le O_H\Bigg(e^{\alpha\gamma/4}\int V_{\phi(a_1)\phi(a_1)}^2+e^{-\alpha\gamma/4}\int V_{\phi(a_2),\phi(b_2)}^2\Bigg),
\end{align*}
using the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality. A similar estimate holds if $\phi(a_2)=\phi(b_2)$. We deduce that
\[|D_{\mathrm{ee}}|\le O_{H}\Bigg(e^{-\alpha \gamma/4}\sum_{i,j}\int V_{i,j}^2+e^{\alpha\gamma/4}\sum_{i}\int V_{ii}^2\Bigg).\]
Similarly,
\begin{align*}|D_{\mathrm{ev}}|&\le O_H\Bigg(   \sqrt{\bigg(\sum_i u_i^2\bigg)\bigg(\sum_i \int V_{ii}^2 + e^{-\alpha \gamma} \sum_{i,j} \int V_{ij}^2\bigg)}\Bigg)\\&\le O_H\Bigg(e^{-\alpha\gamma/4}\sum_i u_i^2+e^{\alpha\gamma/4}\sum_i\int V_{ii}^2+e^{-3\alpha \gamma/4} \sum_{i,j} \int V_{ij}^2\Bigg),\end{align*}
and
    \[
        |D_{\mathrm{vv}}|\le O_H\Bigg(e^{-\alpha \gamma} \sum_i u_i^2\Bigg).
    \]
    Combining all these estimates, we obtain
    \[|\gamma T''(0)|\le e^{-\alpha \gamma/4} \sum_i u_i^2+e^{-\alpha \gamma/5} \sum_i u_i^2+e^{\alpha \gamma/3}\sum_i\int  V_{ii}^2+e^{-\alpha \gamma/5} \sum_{i,j}\int V_{ij}^2,\]
    and combining this with \cref{eq:G''} we obtain $F''_\gamma(0)\ge 0$, as desired.

body_md:
Recall that our objective is to show that $\Psi_\gamma(W)$ is minimised by a function of the form $W_{r,t}^{(k)}$. By \cref{lem:strong-stability}, it suffices to show that $\mathfrak F_\gamma$ is minimised by some $(\mathbf p,\mathbf Q)$ for which $p_1=\dots=p_k=1/k$ and for which each $Q_{ij}$ is a constant-valued function, where the constant value of $Q_{ij}$ only depends on whether $i=j$ or not.

    By \cref{lem:convex}, $\mathfrak F_\gamma$ is convex on its domain $\mathcal Q$. Note that $\mathfrak F_\gamma(\mathbf p,\mathbf Q)$ is symmetric under permutations of the index set $\{1,\dots,k\}$. By convexity, averaging over such permutations cannot increase the value of $\mathfrak F_\gamma$, so there is a minimiser such that $p_1=\dots=p_k$, and $Q_{ii}$ is the same for each $i$, and $Q_{ij}$ is the same for each $i\ne j$. Also, $\mathfrak F_\gamma(\mathbf p,\mathbf Q)$ is symmetric with respect to measure-preserving relabellings $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_k:[0,1]\to [0,1]$ (where we relabel each $Q_{ij}(x,y)$ as $Q_{ij}(\sigma_i(x),\sigma_j(y))$), so a further averaging argument shows that there is a minimiser such that each $Q_{ij}$ is a constant-valued function.

label: def:STS-H
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:STS-H}
Define the graph $G$, the 3-uniform hypergraph $K$ and the
integer $m\in\mathbb N$ in one of the following two ways:
\begin{enumerate}
\item let $G=K_n$ be the complete graph and let $K=K_{n}^{(3)}$ be the complete 3-uniform hypergraph on the same $n$-vertex set (so $|G|=\binom n2$ and $|K|=\binom n3$), and let\footnote{Here we need to assume $\binom n2$ is divisible by 3, or else no Steiner triple system of order $n$ exists.} $m=\binom{n}{2}/3=|G|/3$, or
\item let $G=K_{n,n,n}$ be the complete 3-partite graph and let $K=K_{n,n,n}^{(3)}$ be the complete 3-partite 3-uniform hypergraph on the same $3n$-vertex set (so $|G|=3n^2$ and $|K|=n^3$), and let $m=n^2=|G|/3$.
\end{enumerate}
In both cases, we let $N=|K|$ and define hypergraphs\footnote{Note that vertices of $\mathcal H$ are triples of vertices of $K$. This is slightly confusing, and we will therefore make sure to be consistent with our notation: vertices of $\mathcal H$ will always be denoted with the letters $u,v$, while vertices of $K$ will be denoted with the letters $x,y,z$.} $\mathcal{H}_{4},\mathcal{H}_{2}$
on the vertex set $K$ (i.e., the vertices of $\mathcal{H}_{4},\mathcal{H}_{2}$
are triangles in $G$), as follows. For $\mathcal{H}_{4}$,
put a hyperedge for each Pasch configuration, and for $\mathcal{H}_{2}$,
put a hyperedge for each pair of triples intersecting in a pair of
vertices. Then, let $\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_{4}\cup\mathcal{H}_{2}$
(this is a mixed-uniformity hypergraph, with some hyperedges of size
4 and some hyperedges of size 2).

title: Proof
body_md:
This proof proceeds along similar lines to the proof of \cref{lem:book-deg}; it involves a fairly mechanical consideration of the ways in which pages of both types can intersect a set of fixed vertices and each other. So, we will be brief with details.

First, note that for any $(a,Q)$-book, the $\mathcal H_2$-page vertices are distinct from each other and disjoint from the $\mathcal H_4$-page vertices. For a fixed spine $v=xyz$, there are at most $O(n)$ choices for each $\mathcal H_2$-page vertex, so \cref{eq:book-degrees-goal-1-STS,eq:book-degrees-goal-2-STS} follow directly from \cref{lem:book-deg} (using that $\mathcal H_4$ is $(o(1),O(1);1/n)$-degree-bounded, which can be straightforwardly checked in an analogous way to \cref{prop:H-free}).

For \cref{eq:book-degrees-goal-3-STS}, fix $v_1,\dots,v_s\in \operatorname V(\mathcal H)$; our goal is to upper-bound $\deg_{\operatorname{bk}_k^{a,Q}(\mathcal H)}(v_1,\dots,v_s)$. First, specify which of our fixed vertices should be $\mathcal H_2$-page vertices and which should be $\mathcal H_4$-page vertices (there are $O_A(1)$ ways to make this specification). Let the number of fixed $\mathcal H_2$-page vertices be $t\le |Q|$. We distinguish various cases\footnote{There are various different ways to break down into cases, each of which involves slightly different combinations of estimates. However, none of the ways we tried seemed to yield a really clean proof.} for the values of $t,s$.
\begin{itemize}
    \item If $t=0$ or $s-t\ge 2$, the desired bound follows from \cref{lem:book-deg} (using that there are $O(n)$ choices for each unfixed $\mathcal H_2$-page vertex, given the $\mathcal H_4$-pages).
    \item If $t\ge 2$, note that there are only $O(1)$ possible spines. Indeed, if we write $x_1y_1z_1$ and $x_2y_2z_2$ for two fixed $\mathcal H_2$ page vertices (where at least two of $x_1,x_2,y_1,y_2,z_1,z_2$ must coincide), then the spine $xyz$ must satisfy $\{x,y,z\}\subset\{x_1,x_2,y_1,y_2,z_1,z_2\}$. For each such spine $v=xyz$, the contribution to $\deg_{\operatorname{bk}_k^{a,Q}(\mathcal H)}(v_1,\dots,v_s)$ is at most $O_A(n^{b-(s-t)})\cdot O(n^{|Q|-t})=O_A(1)\cdot(o(1/n))^{s-1}n^k$, where $b=k-|Q|$ is the number of $\mathcal H_4$-page vertices, and we have used a basic overlap-statistics argument as in \cref{eq:book-calculation-for-later} (using $\Delta_\ell(\mathcal H_4)\le O(n^{4-\ell})$) to count the number of choices for the $\mathcal H_4$-pages with a given spine and $s-t$ fixed $\mathcal H_4$-page vertices.
    \item It remains to consider the case where $s\in \{1,2\}$ and $t=1$. There are $O(n)$ choices for the spine, and we can use a basic overlap-statistics argument as in \cref{eq:book-calculation-for-later} to see that the contribution to $\deg_{\operatorname{bk}_k^{a,Q}(\mathcal H)}(v_1,\dots,v_s)$ is at most $O_A(n^{b-(s-t)})\cdot O(n^{|Q|-t})=O_A(n^{k-s})$, so we obtain the bound $\deg_{\operatorname{bk}_k^{a,Q}(\mathcal H)}(v_1,\dots,v_s)\le O_A(n^{k-s+1})$. This is already enough if $s=1$. To improve this bound for $s=2$ (meaning $t=s-t=1$), reorder the pages so that the first $\mathcal H_4$-page contains the unique fixed $\mathcal H_4$-page vertex. After we make a choice for the spine there are at most $\Delta_2(\mathcal H_4)=o(n^2)$ choices for this first $\mathcal H_4$-page (this saves an \(o(1)\)-factor over the basic overlap-statistics bound).
    \qedhere
\end{itemize}

label: lem:STS-reduction-m
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:STS-reduction-m}
For any $\varepsilon>0$, the following holds for sufficiently large $n$. Let $\mathcal H,\mathcal H_4,m$ be as in \cref{def:STS-H}. Then, for $R\sim\operatorname{Unif}(V,m)$,
\[
\log \mathbb P\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big[|\mathcal H[R]|=0\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big]\le  -\min_{\vec{q}}\Big(\operatorname{D}_{\mathrm{KL}}(\vec{q}\,\|\,m/N)+\mathcal H_4(\vec q)\Big)-3m+\varepsilon m,
\]
where the minimum is over all $\vec q\in [0,1]^{\operatorname V(\mathcal H)}$ whose sum of entries is exactly $m$.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $G,K$ be as in \cref{def:STS-H}. For $g\in G$ and a weighting $\vec q=(q_v)_{v\in K}$, write
\[
    \ell_g(\vec q)=\sum_{v\in K:g\subseteq v}q_v.
\]
Also, let $\chi(x)=x+(1-x)\log(1-x)$.

label: lem:STS-reduction-p
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:STS-reduction-p}
For any $\varepsilon,B>0$, there is $N_0\in \mathbb N$ such that the following holds. Let $N\ge N_0$ and let $\mathcal H,\mathcal H_4,G,m$ be as in \cref{def:STS-H}. Then, for\footnote{For this choice of $p$, it is easy to see that $\mathcal H_4$ is $(o(1),O_B(1);p)$-bounded.} $p=Bm/N$ and $R\sim\operatorname{Bin}(V,p)$,
\[
\log \mathbb P\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big[|\mathcal H[R]|=0\text{ and }|R|\le m\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big]\le  -\min_{\vec{q}\in \mathcal Q^*}\Bigg(\operatorname{D}_{\mathrm{KL}}(\vec{q}\,\|\,p)+\mathcal H_4(\vec q)+\sum_{g\in G}\chi(\ell_g(\vec q))\Bigg)+\varepsilon Np,
\]
where $\mathcal Q^*$ is the set of all $\vec q\in [0,p]^{\operatorname V(\mathcal H)}$ whose sum of entries is at most $m$, and which satisfy $\ell_g(\vec q)\in [0,1]$ for each $g\in G$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: The constraint $\ell_g(\vec q)\le 1$ corresponds to the fact that in an independent set $X\subseteq \operatorname V(\mathcal H)$, each pair $g\in G$ can appear in at most one of the triples of $X$. It seems that with a bit more work one can also add a similar constraint $\ell_g(\vec q)=1$ to the statement of \cref{lem:STS-reduction-m}, but this turns out not to be necessary to prove \cref{thm:latin,thm:STS}.

label: lem:moment-STS
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:moment-STS}
For every $M,\beta>0$, there are $A\in\mathbb N$ and $\gamma>0$ such that the
following holds.  Let $\mathcal F$ be a sigma-algebra.  For every $v\in V$, let
$D_v$ be a nonnegative integer-valued random variable, let
$Z_{v,1},Z_{v,2},Z_{v,3}\in\{0,1\}$, and let
$\mu_v,\zeta_{v,1},\zeta_{v,2},\zeta_{v,3}$ be $\mathcal F$-measurable random
variables satisfying $0\le\mu_v\le M$ and $0\le\zeta_{v,i}\le1$.
Suppose that, for every $a\in\{0,\dots,A\}$ and every $Q\subseteq\{1,2,3\}$, we have
\[
\mathbb E\sum_{v\in V}
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left|
 \mathbb E\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left[(D_v)(D_v-1)\dots(D_v-a+1)\prod_{i\in Q}Z_{v,i}\,\middle|\,\mathcal F\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right]
 -\mu_v^a\prod_{i\in Q}\zeta_{v,i}
\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right|
\le\gamma |V|.
\]
Then
\[
\mathbb E\sum_{v\in V}
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left|
 \mathbb P[D_v=Z_{v,1}=Z_{v,2}=Z_{v,3}=0\mid\mathcal F]
 -\exp(-\mu_v)\prod_{i=1}^3(1-\zeta_{v,i})
\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right|
\le\beta |V|.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\zeta_{v,Q}=\prod_{i\in Q}\zeta_{v,i}$ and $Z_{v,Q}=\prod_{i\in Q}Z_{v,i}$, and let 
\[P_{v,Q}=\mathbb E[\mathbbm{1}_{\{D_v=0\}}Z_{v,Q}\,|\,\mathcal F]=\mathbb P[D_v=0\text{ and }Z_{v,i}=1\text{ for }i\in Q\,|\,\mathcal F].\]
Using the Bonferroni inequalities and Taylor's theorem as in the proof of \cref{lem:moment}, we have
    \[|P_{v,Q}-\exp(-\mu_v)\zeta_{v,Q}|\le O_M\Bigg(\frac{M^{A}}{A!}+\sum_{a=0}^A\frac{\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big|\mathbb E[D_v(D_v-1)\dots (D_v-a+1)Z_{v,Q}\,|\,\mathcal F] - \mu_{v}^a\zeta_{v,Q}\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big|}{a!}\Bigg).\]

    Then, by the inclusion-exclusion formula we have
    \[\mathbb P[D_v=Z_{v,1}=Z_{v,2}=Z_{v,3}=0\,|\,\mathcal F]=\sum_{Q\subseteq\{1,2,3\}}(-1)^{|Q|}P_{v,Q}.\]
    Note that
    \[
\sum_{Q\subseteq\{1,2,3\}}(-1)^{|Q|}
\exp(-\mu_v)\zeta_{v,Q}=\exp(-\mu_v)\prod_{i=1}^3(1-\zeta_{v,i}),
\]
so, summing over $v$ and averaging over $\mathcal F$, we obtain
\[
\mathbb E\sum_{v\in V}
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left|
 \mathbb P[D_v=Z_{v,1}=Z_{v,2}=Z_{v,3}=0\mid\mathcal F]
 -\exp(-\mu_v)\prod_{i=1}^3(1-\zeta_{v,i})
\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right|\le  O_M\bigg(\frac{M^{A}}{A!}+e\gamma\bigg)|V|.
\]
The desired result follows, assuming $A$ is sufficiently large in terms of $\beta,M$ and $\gamma>0$ is sufficiently small in terms of $\beta$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Throughout this proof we view $B$ as a fixed constant (so all asymptotic notation and parameter choices may implicitly depend on $B$).

We proceed in a similar way to \cref{subsec:independent-example}, so we will be brief with details that we have already seen there. We will need auxiliary parameters $T,A,\gamma,\xi,\alpha,\beta,\theta,C_0$, chosen in exactly the same order as in \cref{subsec:independent-example}. In addition to the dependencies listed there, we also need $\beta$ to be small in terms of $T$. 

\medskip\noindent
\textit{Step 1: Reducing to an entropic problem.}
Recall that $\operatorname V(\mathcal H)=K$. Let $\mathcal D=\{S\subseteq K:|\mathcal H[S]|\le 0\text{ and }|S|\le m\}$, and let $Y$ be a sample from the conditional distribution of $R\sim\operatorname{Bin}(K,p)$ given $R\in\mathcal D$. Apply \cref{thm:KS} with parameters $r_0=3A+3$ and $\alpha,\xi,C_0$ to obtain a set $W\subseteq K$. For any possible outcome $U$ of $Y\cap W$ we let
\[\operatorname H^{U}[Y]=\operatorname H[Y\,|\,Y\cap W=U],\quad q_v^U=\mathbb P[v\in Y\,|\,Y\cap W=U],\]
and we obtain
\begin{align}
\log \mathbb P[|\mathcal H[R]|=0\text{ and }|R|\le m]&= -\operatorname D_{\mathrm{KL}}\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big(\mathcal L(Y\cap W) \,\|\, \mathrm{Bin}(W,p)\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big) \notag\\
&\qquad\qquad + \operatorname H[Y\,|\,Y\cap W]+\sum_{v\in K\setminus W} \Big(\mathbb P[v\in Y]\log p + \mathbb P[v\notin Y]\log(1-p)\Big)\notag\\
& \le \mathbb E\Bigg[ \operatorname H^{Y\cap W}[Y] +\sum_{v\in K\setminus W} \Big(q^{Y\cap W}_v\log p + (1-q^{Y\cap W}_v)\log(1-p)\Big)\Bigg].\label{eq:average-entropy-STS}
\end{align}

\medskip\noindent
\textit{Step 2: Sequential entropy.}
Fix any outcome $U$ of $Y\cap W$, and let $X$ have the conditional
distribution of $Y\setminus W$ given $Y\cap W=U$, so $\operatorname H^{U}[Y]=\operatorname H[X]$. Let $q_v=q^U_v=\mathbb P[v\in X]$ for $v\notin W$, and $q_v=0$ for $v\in W$.

We now need some new parameters to describe the different types of ``threats'' from hyperedges of $\mathcal H_2$ or $\mathcal H_4$. For $S\subseteq K\setminus W$ and $v\in K\setminus W$:
\begin{itemize}
    \item Similarly to \cref{subsec:independent-example}, let $D_v(S)$ be the number of hyperedges $e\in \mathcal H_4$ such that $v\in e$ and $e\setminus v\subseteq S$;
    \item for $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ define $Z_{v,i}(S)\in \{0,1\}$ by letting $Z_{v,i}(S)=1$ if $v[i]\subseteq u$ for some $u\in S\setminus v$.
\end{itemize}
Note that if $v\notin S$ and at least one of $D_v(S),Z_{v,1}(S),Z_{v,2}(S),Z_{v,3}(S)$ is nonzero, then augmenting $\mathcal H[S]$ with $v$ would introduce a hyperedge (of $\mathcal H_4$ or $\mathcal H_2$, respectively). Let $\operatorname{ex}(S)$ be the set of $v\in K\setminus W$ such that $D_v(S)=Z_{v,1}(S)=Z_{v,2}(S)=Z_{v,3}(S)=0$, let $V_1\cup\dots\cup V_T$ be a uniformly random partition of $K\setminus W$, let $X_t=X\cap V_t$ and let \[b_v(t)=b_v^U(t)=\mathbb P[v\in \operatorname{ex}(X_{<t})]=\mathbb P[D_v(X_{<t})=Z_{v,1}(X_{<t})=Z_{v,2}(X_{<t})=Z_{v,3}(X_{<t})=0].\] By \cref{lem:seq-ent}, we have
\begin{equation}
    \operatorname H[X]\le \frac 1T\sum_{t =1}^{T}\sum_{v\in K\setminus W}q_v\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big(1-\log q_v+\log b_v(t)\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big).\label{eq:seq-ent-application-STS}
\end{equation} 
Now, 
let \[\mu_v(t)=\mu_v^U(t)=\Big(\frac{t-1}T\Big)^{3}\sum_{\substack{e\in \mathcal H_4[K\setminus W]:\\v\in e}}\;\prod_{u\in e\setminus v}q_{u},\qquad \zeta_{v,i}(t)=\zeta_{v,i}^U(t)=\frac{t-1}T\cdot \ell_{v[i]}(\vec q)\]
and
\[\tilde  b_v(t)=\tilde b_v^U(t)=\exp(-\mu_v(t))\prod_{i=1}^3(1-\zeta_{v,i}(t)).\]

\medskip \noindent\textit{Step 3: Elementary estimates.}
As in \cref{subsec:independent-example}, by Harris' inequality and $(o(1),O_B(1);p)$-degree-boundedness of $\mathcal H_4$, we have $\mu_v(t)\le p^{3}\Delta_1(\mathcal H_4)=O_B(1)$. Also note that $(t-1)/T\le1-1/T$ and
$\ell_g(\vec q)=\mathbb E|\{v\in X:g\subseteq v\}|\le1$ for all $g\in G$, so
\begin{equation}
    \tilde b_v(t)\ge \exp(-O(1))/T^3=\Omega_{T}(1).\label{eq:nondegenerate-probability-STS}
\end{equation}
As in
\cref{subsec:independent-example}, considering separately the cases
$b_v(t)\le\tilde b_v(t)$ and
$b_v(t)>\tilde b_v(t)$ yields
\[
 \log b_v(t)-\log\tilde b_v(t)
 \le O_{T}(|b_v(t)-\tilde b_v(t)|),
\]
so we deduce from \cref{eq:seq-ent-application-STS} that
\begin{align}&\operatorname H[X] +\sum_{v\in K\setminus W} \mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big(q_v\log p + (1-q_v)\log(1-p)\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big)\notag\\
&\qquad\qquad\le \sum_{v\in K\setminus W}\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big(q_v-q_v\log q_v+q_v\log p+(1-q_v)\log(1-p)\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big) \notag\\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad +\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{v\in K\setminus W} q_v \log \tilde b_{v}(t)
+ O_T\Bigg(\sum_{t=1}^Tp\sum_{v\in K\setminus W}|b_{v}(t)-\tilde b_{v}(t)|\Bigg).\label{eq:H-expansion-STS}
\end{align}
Let $\vec q=(q_v)_{v\in K}\in [0,p]^K$. Note that $\sum_v q_v\le \mathbb E |X|\le m$ and $\ell_g(\vec q)=\mathbb E|\{v\in X:g\subseteq v\}|\le1$ by the definition of $X$ via $Y$, so $\vec q\in \mathcal Q^*$.
Exactly as in \cref{eq:H-KL-independent}, we have
\begin{align}&\sum_{v\in K\setminus W}\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big(q_v-q_v\log q_v+q_v\log p+(1-q_v)\log(1-p)\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big)\notag\\
&\qquad \le -\operatorname D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\vec q\,\|\,p)+O(p^2 N)+O(p|W|)\le -\operatorname D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\vec q\,\|\,p)+(\varepsilon/5)pN,\label{eq:H-KL-STS}\end{align}
and as in \cref{eq:H-mean-independent} we have
\begin{equation}\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{v\in K\setminus W} q_v \cdot (-\mu_{v}(t))\le -\mathcal H_4(\vec q)+(\varepsilon/5) pN.\label{eq:H-mean-STS}\end{equation}
Compared to \cref{subsec:independent-example}, we also need to consider some additional terms, due to the slightly more complicated definition of $\tilde b_v(t)$. Indeed, note that
\[
\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{v\in K}q_v
 \sum_{i=1}^3\log\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big(1-\zeta_{v,i}(t)\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big)
=\sum_{g\in G} \frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T
 \ell_g(\vec q)\log\Big(1-\frac{t-1}{T}\cdot \ell_g(\vec q)\Big).
 \]
 By a Riemann sum approximation we have 
 \[\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T
 \ell_g(\vec q)\log\Big(1-\frac{t-1}{T}\cdot \ell_g(\vec q)\Big)=\int_0^1\ell_g(\vec q)\log(1-z\ell_g(\vec q))\,dz+o_{T\to\infty}(1)=-\chi(\ell_g(\vec q))+o_{T\to\infty}(1),\]
 so
 \begin{equation}
     \frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{v\in K}q_v
 \sum_{i=1}^3\log\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big(1-\zeta_{v,i}(t)\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big)=-\sum_{g\in G}\chi(\ell_g(\vec q))+o_{T\to \infty}(m).\label{eq:pair-cost-STS}
 \end{equation}
 Combining
\cref{eq:seq-ent-application-STS,eq:H-KL-STS,eq:H-mean-STS,eq:pair-cost-STS,eq:H-expansion-STS}, we deduce
\begin{align}&\operatorname H[X] +\sum_{v\in K\setminus W} \mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big(q_v\log p + (1-q_v)\log(1-p)\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big)\notag\\
& \le -\min_{\vec{q}\in \mathcal Q^*}\Bigg(\operatorname{D}_{\mathrm{KL}}(\vec{q}\,\|\,p)+\mathcal H_4(\vec q)+\sum_{g\in G}\chi(\ell_g(\vec q))\Bigg)+O_T\Bigg(\sum_{t=1}^Tp\sum_{v\in K\setminus W}|b_{v}(t)-\tilde b_{v}(t)|\Bigg)+(\varepsilon/2)pN.\label{eq:conditional-with-random-error-STS}\end{align}

\medskip\noindent
\textit{Step 4: Joint Bernoulli/Poisson approximation.}
It remains to control the final term in
\cref{eq:conditional-with-random-error-STS}. We proceed similarly to \cref{subsec:independent-example}, using \cref{lem:moment-STS} instead of \cref{lem:moment}. This requires a few additional estimates.

Let $\operatorname{bk}^{a,Q}(\mathcal H[K\setminus W];v)=\bigcup_{k}\operatorname{bk}^{a,Q}_k(\mathcal H[K\setminus W];v)$ and observe that
\begin{align}
&\mathbb E\Bigg[D_v(X_{<t})(D_v(X_{<t})-1)\dots(D_v(X_{<t})-a+1)\prod_{i\in Q}Z_{v,i}(X_{<t})\Bigg]\notag\\
&\qquad=\sum_{e\in \operatorname{bk}^{a,Q}(\mathcal H[K\setminus W];v)}\mathbb E[\mathbbm{1}_{e\subseteq X_{<t}}]\notag\\
&\qquad=\sum_{k=0}^{3a+|Q|}\bigg(\frac{t-1}T\bigg)^k\sum_{e\in \operatorname{bk}^{a,Q}_k(\mathcal H[K\setminus W];v)}\mathbb E[\mathbbm{1}_{e\subseteq X}].\label{eq:falling-factorial-STS}\end{align}

Next, let $q_e(t)=((t-1)/T)^{|e|}\prod_{u\in e}q_u$. To apply the conclusion of \cref{thm:KS}, we need to estimate
\[\sum_{k=0}^{3a+|Q|}\bigg(\frac{t-1}T\bigg)^k\sum_{e\in \operatorname{bk}^{a,Q}_k(\mathcal H[K\setminus W];v)}\;\prod_{u\in e}\mathbb E[\mathbbm{1}_{u\in  X}]=\sum_{e\in \operatorname{bk}^{a,Q}(\mathcal H[K\setminus W];v)}q_e(t).\]
For this, note that for each $(a,Q)$-book, the page vertices corresponding to $\mathcal H_2$ are distinct from the page vertices corresponding to $\mathcal H_4$. So, we can break down the above sum over $e\in \operatorname{bk}^{a,Q}$ into two separate sums over the two different types of pages. Indeed, recalling \cref{def:books} we have
\[\sum_{e\in \operatorname{bk}^{a,Q}(\mathcal H[K\setminus W];v)}q_e(t)=\Bigg(\prod_{i\in Q}\;\sum_{\substack{u\in K\setminus v:\\u\supseteq v[i]}}q_u(t)\Bigg)\Bigg(\sum_{e\in \operatorname{bk}^{a}(\mathcal H_4[K\setminus W];v)}q_e(t)\Bigg).\]
Recall from \cref{subsec:independent-example} that
\[
\sum_{e\in \operatorname{bk}^{a}(\mathcal H_4[K\setminus W];v)}q_e(t)=\mu_v(t)^a\pm \gamma/2
\]
and, recalling that $q_v\le p$, note that
\[\sum_{\substack{u\in K\setminus v:\\u\supseteq v[i]}}q_u(t)=\frac{t-1}T\cdot(\ell_{v[i]}(\vec q)-q_v)= \zeta_{v,i}(t)\pm o(1).\]
Recalling that $\mu_v(t)\le O(1)$, we deduce
\begin{equation}
    \sum_{k=0}^{3a+|Q|}\bigg(\frac{t-1}T\bigg)^k\sum_{e\in \operatorname{bk}^{a,Q}_k(\mathcal H[K\setminus W];v)}\;\prod_{u\in e}\mathbb E[\mathbbm{1}_{u\in  X}]=\mu_v(t)^a\prod_{i\in Q}\zeta_{v,i}(t)\pm (2\gamma/3)\label{eq:product-independent-STS}
\end{equation}
Then, the conclusion of \cref{thm:KS} (recalling \cref{lem:book-degrees-STS} to verify the condition \cref{eq:KS-degree-condition}) implies that 
\[
\mathbb E\sum_{v\in K\setminus W} \Bigg|
\sum_{k=0}^{3a+|Q|}\bigg(\frac{t-1}T\bigg)^k\sum_{e\in \operatorname{bk}^{a,Q}_k(\mathcal H[K\setminus W];v)}\bigg(\mathbb E[\mathbbm{1}_{e\subseteq Y}\,|\,Y\cap W]-\prod_{u\in e}\mathbb E[\mathbbm{1}_{u\in Y}\,|\,Y\cap W]\bigg)\Bigg|
\le  (3a+3)\xi N
\]
which is at most $(\gamma/3)N$ (recalling that $\xi$ is small in terms of $\gamma,A$). For all $t$ let $Y_t=(Y\setminus W)\cap V_t$ and $Y_{<t}=Y_1\cup \dots\cup Y_{t-1}$, so  $X_{<t}$ has the distribution of $Y_{<t}$ given $Y\cap W=U$. Substituting \cref{eq:falling-factorial-STS,eq:product-independent-STS} into the above inequality, we obtain
\begin{align*}
&\mathbb E\sum_{v\in K\setminus W} \Bigg|\mathbb E\Bigg[D_v(Y_{<t})(D_v(Y_{<t})-1)\dots(D_v(Y_{<t})-a+1)\prod_{i\in Q}Z_{v,i}(Y_{<t})\,\Bigg|\,Y\cap W\Bigg]\\
&\qquad\qquad \qquad -\mu_v^{Y\cap W}(t)^a\prod_{i\in Q}\zeta^{Y\cap W}_{v,i}(t)\Bigg| \le  \gamma N,
\end{align*}
so by \cref{lem:moment-STS} (with $\mathcal F$ being the $\sigma$-algebra generated by $Y\cap W$) we have
\begin{align*}
    &\mathbb E\sum_{v\in K\setminus W}|b_v^{Y\cap W}(t)-\tilde b_v^{Y\cap W}(t)|\\
    &\qquad =\mathbb E\sum_{v\in K\setminus W}\Bigg|\mathbb P[D_v(Y_{<t})=Z_{v,1}(Y_{<t})=Z_{v,2}(Y_{<t})=Z_{v,3}(Y_{<t})=0\,|\,Y\cap W]\\
    &\qquad\qquad\qquad \qquad\qquad  -\exp(-\mu_v^{Y\cap W}(t))\prod_{i=1}^3(1-\zeta^{Y\cap W}_{v,i}(t))\Bigg|\le \beta N.
\end{align*}
The desired result then follows by combining this with \cref{eq:conditional-with-random-error-STS,eq:average-entropy-STS} (and using our new assumption that $\beta$ is small with respect to $T$, in addition to $\varepsilon$).

label: lem:sidorenko-K222
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:sidorenko-K222}For any $u:[n]^{3}\to[0,\infty)$, we have
\[
\mathbb E_{x_{0},y_{0},z_{0},x_{1},y_{1},z_{1}}\prod_{i,j,k\in\{0,1\}}u(x_{i},y_{j},z_{k})\ge(\mathbb E_{x,y,z}u(x,y,z))^{8}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof is just by iterated application of the Cauchy--Schwarz
inequality (over $x$, then $y$, then $z$). First,
\[
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb E_{x,y,z}u(x,y,z)\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{2}\le\mathbb E_{y,z}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb E_{x}u(x,y,z)\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{2}=\mathbb E_{x_{0},x_{1},y,z}\prod_{i\in\{0,1\}}u(x_{i},y,z).
\]
Then
\[
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb E_{x_{0},x_{1},y,z}\prod_{i\in\{0,1\}}u(x_{i},y,z)\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{2}\le\mathbb E_{x_{0},x_{1},z}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb E_{y}\prod_{i\in\{0,1\}}u(x_{i},y,z)\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{2}=\mathbb E_{x_{0},x_{1},z}\mathbb E_{y_{0},y_{1}}\prod_{i,j\in\{0,1\}}u(x_{i},y_{j},z).
\]
Finally,
\begin{align*}
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb E_{x_{0},x_{1},y_{0},y_{1},z}\prod_{i,j\in\{0,1\}}u(x_{i},y_{j},z)\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{2}&\le\mathbb E_{x_{0},x_{1},y_{0},y_{1}}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb E_{z}\prod_{i,j\in\{0,1\}}u(x_{i},y_{j},z)\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)^{2}\\&=\mathbb E_{x_{0},x_{1},y_{0},y_{1},z_{0},z_{1}}\prod_{i,j,k\in\{0,1\}}u(x_{i},y_{j},z_{k}).
\end{align*}
The desired result follows.

label: lem:STS-analytic
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:STS-analytic}
Consider $w:[n]^{3}\to[0,\infty)$ satisfying $\mathbb E_{x,y,z}w(x,y,z)=1$.
Then
\[
\mathbb E_{x,y,z}\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big[w(x,y,z)\log w(x,y,z)\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big]+\frac{1}{4}\mathbb E_{*}\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big[w(x_{0},y_{0},z_{0})w(x_{1},y_{1},z_{0})w(x_{1},y_{0},z_{1})w(x_{0},y_{1},z_{1})\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big]\ge\frac{1}{4},
\]
where we write ``$\mathbb E_{*}$'' as shorthand for ``$\mathbb E_{x_{0},y_{0},z_{0},x_{1},y_{1},z_{1}}$''.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First, let 
\[
W=\prod_{i,j,k\in\{0,1\}}w(x_{i},y_{j},z_{k}),\quad W_{0}=\prod_{\substack{i,j,k\in\{0,1\}\\
i+j+k\text{ even}
}
}w(x_{i},y_{j},z_{k}),\quad W_{1}=\prod_{\substack{i,j,k\in\{0,1\}\\
i+j+k\text{ odd}
}
}w(x_{i},y_{j},z_{k}).
\]
By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and symmetry, we have
\[
\mathbb E_{*}\sqrt{W}=\mathbb E_{*}\sqrt{W_{0}W_{1}}\le\sqrt{\mathbb E_{*}W_{0}\mathbb E_{*}W_{1}}=\mathbb E_{*}W_{0}.
\]
So, by \cref{lem:sidorenko-K222}, we have 
\[
(\mathbb E_{*}W_{0})^{1/8}\ge\mathbb E_{x,y,z}\sqrt{w(x,y,z)}.
\]

Then, using Jensen's inequality with respect to the probability measure
$(x,y,z)\mapsto w(x,y,z)/n^{3}$ (recalling that $\mathbb E_{x,y,z}w(x,y,z)=1$), we have
\begin{align*}
\log\mathbb E_{x,y,z}\sqrt{w(x,y,z)}=\log\mathbb E_{x,y,z}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left[w(x,y,z)w(x,y,z)^{-1/2}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right]&\ge\mathbb E_{x,y,z}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left[w(x,y,z)\log(w(x,y,z)^{-1/2})\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right]\\
&=-\frac{1}{2}\mathbb E_{x,y,z}\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big[w(x,y,z)\log w(x,y,z)\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big].
\end{align*}
(This is essentially monotonicity of R\'enyi divergence; see \cite{Ren60}). Combining these inequalities yields
\[
\mathbb E_{x,y,z}\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big[w(x,y,z)\log w(x,y,z)\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big]\ge-2\log\mathbb E_{x,y,z}\sqrt{w(x,y,z)}\ge-\frac{1}{4}\log\mathbb E_{*}W_{1},
\]
so
\[
\mathbb E_{x,y,z}\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big[w(x,y,z)\log w(x,y,z)\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big]+\frac{1}{4}\mathbb E_{*}W_{1}\ge\frac{1}{4}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(-\log\mathbb E_{*}W_{1}+\mathbb E_{*}W_{1}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)\ge\frac{1}{4},
\]
using that 1 is the minimum value of $-\log u+u$, over $u\in[0,\infty)$.

title: Proof
body_md:
We only need to prove the upper bound, as the lower bound was already proved by Kwan, Sah, Sawhney and Simkin~\cite[Theorem~1.1]{KSSS23}. We work in setting (2) of \cref{def:STS-H}.

Let $\vec q=(q_{xyz})_{xyz\in K_{n,n,n}^{(3)}}$ be a weighting which minimises $\operatorname D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\vec{q}\,\|\,m/N)+\mathcal{H}_{4}(\vec{q})$, over all such weightings with sum of entries exactly $m$. By \cref{lem:truncation-lower} we have $q_{xyz}\le O(m/N)=O(1/n)$ for all $xyz\in K_{n,n,n}^{(3)}$. The same estimates as in the previous proof yield
\begin{align*}
\operatorname D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\vec{q}\,\|\,m/N)+\mathcal{H}_{4}(\vec{q}) & \ge
\sum_{x,y,z\in [n]}q_{xyz}\log\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac{q_{x,y,z}}{m/N}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)-\sum_{x,y,z\in [n]}q_{xyz}+\sum_{x,y,z\in [n]}\frac m N\\
&\qquad+\frac{1}{4}\sum_{x_0,x_1,y_0,y_1,z_0,z_1\in [n]
}q_{x_0y_0z_0}q_{x_1y_1z_0}q_{x_1y_0z_1}q_{x_0y_1z_1}+o(m),
\end{align*}
where we have used that there are $8/2=4$ automorphisms of a Pasch configuration that respect its natural tripartition.

Letting $w(x,y,z)=q_{x,y,z}/(m/N)$ (and recalling that $m=n^2$ and $N=n^3$), we can rewrite the above expression as
\[m\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(
\mathbb E_{x,y,z}\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big[w(x,y,z)\log w(x,y,z)\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big]+\frac{1}{4}\mathbb E_{*}\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big[w(x_{0},y_{0},z_{0})w(x_{1},y_{1},z_{0})w(x_{1},y_{0},z_{1})w(x_{0},y_{1},z_{1})\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big]\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)+o(m).\]
The desired result then follows from \cref{lem:STS-reduction-m,lem:STS-analytic}.

label: lem:KS-simultaneous-regularisation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:KS-simultaneous-regularisation}
Consider $K,r_0,\alpha,\beta>0$. There exists $\theta>0$ and
$N_0\in\mathbb N$ such that the following holds.  Let $p\in(0,1/2)$ and $N=|V|\ge N_0$ and let $Y$ be a sample from $\operatorname{Bin}(V,p)$, conditioned on a nonempty decreasing event $\mathcal D$.  Then there is $W\subseteq V$ with $|W|\le \alpha N$
such that
\[
 \mathcal E_{\mathcal G}(W)\le\beta e(\mathcal G)
 \qquad\text{for every }\mathcal G\in \mathfrak G_{\mathrm{KS}}(K,\theta).
\]
head: environment

label: eq:KS-parameter-choice
title: Proof
body_md:
We may assume that $\alpha<1/2$, $\beta<1$ and $K>1$. As in the proof of \cite[Lemma~18]{KS23}, define the parameters
\begin{equation}\label{eq:KS-parameter-choice}
 \gamma=\frac{\beta^2}{300Kr_0},
 \qquad
 \tau=\frac{\alpha\gamma}2,
 \qquad
 \theta=\frac{\tau}{2r_0},\qquad N_0=8r_0^2/\tau
\end{equation}
Let
$i_p(q)=q\log(q/p)+(1-q)\log((1-q)/(1-p))$, and for $W\subseteq V$ let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:KS-potential-small-p}
 \mathcal I(W)=\sum_{v\in V\setminus W}\mathbb E\,i_p(\mathbb E_WY_v).
\end{equation}
Note that, writing $R_p\sim\operatorname{Bin}(V,p)$ (and recalling $p\le 1/2$), we have
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal I(W)\le
 \operatorname{D}_{\mathrm{KL}}\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big(\mathcal L(Y)\,\|\,\operatorname{Bin}(V,p)\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big)
 =-\log\mathbb P[R_p\in \mathcal D]\le -\log\mathbb P[R_p=\emptyset]=N\log(1/(1-p))\le 2pN. \label{eq:I(W)-KS}
\end{equation}

We will build our set $W$ in several rounds, starting with $W$ being the empty set. In each round we will use the following claim, which appears as \cite[Claim~19]{KS23}.

\begin{claim}\label{clm:KS-increment}
    Fix an edge-weighted hypergraph $\mathcal G\in \mathfrak G_{\mathrm{KS}}(K,\theta)$. Suppose that $W\subseteq V$ satisfies $\mathcal E_\mathcal G(W)> \beta e(\mathcal G)$, and $|V\setminus W|\ge N_0/2$. Then there is $W'\subseteq V\setminus W$ with size at most $\tau|V|$ such that 
    \[\mathcal I(W\cup W')\ge \mathcal I(W)+\gamma p|V|.\]
\end{claim}

Now, we show how to use \cref{clm:KS-increment} to complete the proof of \cref{lem:KS-simultaneous-regularisation}. Suppose for the purpose of contradiction that there is no set $W$ with at most $\alpha N$ elements  such that $\mathcal E_\mathcal G(W)\le \beta e(\mathcal G)$ for every $\mathcal G\in \mathfrak G_{\mathrm{KS}}(K,\theta)$. Let $j=\lfloor\alpha/\tau\rfloor+1$; we construct sets $W_0,\dots,W_j$ such that, for every
$i\in\{0,\dots,j\}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:KS-iteration-properties}
 |W_i|\le i\tau N
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 \mathcal I(W_i)\ge i\gamma pN.
\end{equation}
If such a sequence existed, we would have
\[\mathcal I(W_j)\ge j\cdot \gamma p|V|,\]which would contradict \cref{eq:I(W)-KS}.

Start with $W_0=\emptyset$.  Suppose that $i\le j-1$ and $W_i$ has been
constructed to satisfy the desired properties.  Then
\[
 |W_i|\le i\tau N
 \le\lfloor\alpha/\tau\rfloor\tau N
 \le\alpha N,
\]
so, by assumption, there is some $\mathcal G_i\in \mathfrak G_{\mathrm{KS}}(K,\theta)$ such that $\mathcal E_{\mathcal G_i}(W_i)>\beta e(\mathcal G_i)$.  Moreover, $
 |V\setminus W_i|\ge(1-\alpha)N>N/2\ge N_0/2
$.
Let $W'\subseteq V\setminus W_i$ be the set obtained by applying \cref{clm:KS-increment} with $W_i$ and $\mathcal G_i$, and put
$W_{i+1}=W_i\cup W'$.  Then \cref{eq:KS-iteration-properties} continues
to hold with $i+1$ in place of $i$.  This proves the lemma.

label: clm:KS-increment
title: Claim
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $K$ be large in terms of $C_0,\xi$, and let $\beta$ be small in terms of $C_0,\xi$. Let $\theta,N_0$ be as in \cref{lem:KS-simultaneous-regularisation}.

Choose $W\subseteq V$ with $|W|\le\alpha N$, such that $\mathcal E_{\mathcal G}(W)\le\beta e(\mathcal G)$ for every $\mathcal G\in \mathfrak G_{\mathrm{KS}}(K,\theta)$. We claim that the desired condition holds for this $W$.

For a weighted $k$-uniform $\mathcal G\in\mathfrak G(C_0,\theta)$, call $\mathcal G$
\emph{relevant} if 
$p^k e(\mathcal G)>(\xi/2)N$. 
First, observe that for every $e\in \mathcal G\in \mathfrak G(C_0,\theta)$ we have
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E\bigg|\mathbb E_W[Y_e]-\prod_{v\in e}\mathbb E_W[Y_v]\bigg|
 \le2p^{|e|}
\end{equation*}
by \cref{lem:harris}. So, for every $k$-uniform non-relevant $\mathcal G\in \mathfrak G(C_0,\theta)$ we have
\[
 \mathbb E\Bigg[
 \sum_{e\in\mathcal G[V\setminus W]}\operatorname{wt}_{\mathcal G}(e)
 \bigg|\mathbb E_W[Y_e]-\prod_{v\in e}\mathbb E_W[Y_v]\bigg|
 \Bigg]
 \le2p^k e(\mathcal G)\le\xi N.
\]
On the other hand, for any $k$-uniform relevant $\mathcal G\in \mathfrak G(C_0,\theta)$, we have $\mathcal G\in \mathfrak G_{\mathrm{KS}}(K,\theta)$ (since $K$ is large in terms of $C_0,\xi$), so we can apply the conclusion of \cref{lem:KS-simultaneous-regularisation}. Note that
\[
 k e(\mathcal G)=\sum_{v\in V}\deg_{\mathcal G}(v)
 \le N\Delta_1(\mathcal G)\le C_0Np^{-k},
\]
so \cref{lem:KS-energy-controls-products} and the conclusion of \cref{lem:KS-simultaneous-regularisation} give
\[
 \mathbb E\Bigg[
 \sum_{A\in\mathcal G[V\setminus W]}\operatorname{wt}_{\mathcal G}(A)
 \bigg|\mathbb E_W[Y_A]-\prod_{v\in A}\mathbb E_W[Y_v]\bigg|
 \Bigg]\le p^ke(\mathcal G)\sqrt{(k-1)\beta}\le \frac{C_0\sqrt{(k-1)\beta}}k N\le \xi N
\]
(recalling that $\beta$ is small in terms of $C_0,\xi$). So, both non-relevant and relevant $\mathcal G\in \mathfrak G(C_0,\theta)$ satisfy the desired inequality.

label: claim:app-prob-upper
title: Claim
body_md:
\label{claim:app-prob-upper}
Consider any sequence of independent sets $J_1\subseteq \dots\subseteq J_\ell$.
Then
\[\log \mathbb P[(I_1,\dots,I_\ell)=(J_1,\dots,J_\ell)\text{ and }\mathcal E\text{ occurs}]\le -\log \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\ell^{|J_\ell|}\binom N{|J_\ell|}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)+\Lambda(J_1,\dots,J_\ell)+o(\alpha N),\]
where
\[\Lambda(J_1,\dots,J_\ell)=\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}\sum_{v\in J_{i+1}\setminus J_{i}}\deg(v)\sum_{h=0}^{i-1}p_h\chi_h.\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For each $i$, let $M_i$ be a random subset of $\Gamma_i$ obtained by including each element with probability $\theta=1-1/\log \log f=1-o(1)$. Let $J_{i+1}^*=J_{i+1}\setminus J_{i}$ (taking $J_0=\emptyset$). Then, for any outcome of $\Gamma_1,\dots,\Gamma_\ell$ we have \begin{align*}&\mathbb P[(M_1,\dots,M_\ell)=(J_1^*,\dots,J_\ell^*)\text{ and }\mathcal E\text{ occurs}\,|\,\Gamma_1,\dots,\Gamma_\ell]\\
&\qquad \ge \prod_{i=1}^\ell \theta^{|J_i^*|}(1-\theta)^{|\Gamma_i|-|J_i^*|}\cdot \mathbb P[(I_1,\dots,I_\ell)=(J_1,\dots,J_\ell)\text{ and }\mathcal E\text{ occurs}\,|\,\Gamma_1,\dots,\Gamma_\ell]\\
&\qquad \ge \theta^{|J_\ell|}(1-\theta)^{|J_\ell|/\log f}\cdot \mathbb P[(I_1,\dots,I_\ell)=(J_1,\dots,J_\ell)\text{ and }\mathcal E\text{ occurs}\,|\,\Gamma_1,\dots,\Gamma_\ell]\\
&\qquad \ge \exp(-o(\alpha N))\cdot  \mathbb P[(I_1,\dots,I_\ell)=(J_1,\dots,J_\ell)\text{ and }\mathcal E\text{ occurs}\,|\,\Gamma_1,\dots,\Gamma_\ell].\end{align*}
(Here we used $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{\ref{lem:Gamma-approx-I}}}$).
So, it suffices to show that 
\[\log \mathbb P[(M_1,\dots,M_\ell)=(J_1^*,\dots,J_\ell^*)\text{ and }\mathcal E\text{ occurs}]\le -\log \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\ell^{|J_\ell|}
\binom N{|J_\ell|}
\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)+\Lambda(J_1,\dots,J_\ell)+o(\alpha N).\]

To have $(M_1,\dots,M_\ell)=(J_1^*,\dots,J_\ell^*)$, it must be the case that for each $i+1\le \ell$:
\begin{itemize}
    \item For each $v\in J_{i+1}^*$ we have $v\in M_{i+1}$,
    \item For each $v\in A_i\setminus J_{i+1}^*$ we have $v\notin M_{i+1}$,
    \item For each $v\in J_\ell\setminus J_{i+1}$ we have $v\notin S_{i+1}$.
\end{itemize}
If we condition on any outcome of the process up to step $i$ (consistent with $\mathcal X_i$, recalling \cref{lem:GW-good-events}(1)), these bullet points jointly occur with probability at most
\[(\theta p_i)^{|J_{i+1}^*|}(1-\theta p_i)^{|A_i|-|J_{i+1}^*|}\prod_{v\in J_\ell\setminus J_{i+1}}(1-\hat p_{v,i})\le p_i^{|J_{i+1}^*|}(1-\theta p_i)^{a_i-|J_{i+1}^*|}\prod_{v\in J_\ell\setminus J_{i+1}}(1-p_{i})^{K_i-y_v(i)},\]
where $a_i=(1-1/\log f)q_i N$ and $y_v(i)=\chi_i(\deg(v)+D/(\log f)^2)$.
So, multiplying over all steps and re-indexing,  
we see that
\[\mathbb P[(M_1,\dots,M_\ell)=(J_1^*,\dots,J_\ell^*)\text{ and }\mathcal E\text{ occurs}]\le \prod_{i=0}^{\ell-1}(1-\theta p_i)^{a_i-|J_{i+1}^*|}\prod_{v\in J_{i+1}^*}p_i\prod_{h=0}^{i-1}(1-p_{h})^{K_h-y_v(h)}\]
(here we are using $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{\ref{lem:app-Y-size}}}$ and property (2) in \cref{lem:GW-good-events}).
The logarithm of this is at most
\begin{equation}
    \sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}\Bigg(-(a_i-|J_{i+1}^*|)\theta p_i+\sum_{v\in J_{i+1}^*}\bigg(\log p_i-\sum_{h=0}^{i-1}\Big(p_{h}K_h-p_{h}y_v(h)\Big)\bigg)\Bigg).\label{eq:semi-random-intermediate}
\end{equation}
Now, it basically remains to simplify this expression, recalling the definitions of all the relevant parameters. First, we have
\[\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1} (a_i-|J_{i+1}^*|)\theta p_i=\frac{\ell \sigma N}{D^{1/(r-1)}}+o(\alpha N)=\alpha N+o(\alpha N),\]
using that 
\begin{equation}
\ell\sigma=\xi(\log f)^{1/(r-1)}+O(\sigma),\quad D^{1/(r-1)}=(1-o(1))\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac{N}{|J_\ell|}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)\xi(\log f)^{1/(r-1)}.\label{eq:recall-parameters}
\end{equation}
Then, by a Riemann sum approximation we have
\[\sum_{h=0}^{i-1}p_{h}K_h=\sigma(r-1)\sum_{h=0}^{i-1}\pi_h^{r-2}+O\Big(\sigma^{1+\rho}\sum_{h=0}^{i-1}\pi_h^{\max(r-3,0)}\Big)=(i\sigma)^{r-1}+o(1).\]
We also have the cruder estimate
\[\sum_{h=0}^{i-1}p_h\chi_h=\frac{r-1}D\sum_{h=0}^{i-1}\sigma \pi_h^{r-2}\le \frac{r-1}D\ell\sigma(\ell\sigma)^{r-2}\le \frac{(r-1)\xi^{r-1}\log f}D\](where we again recall \cref{eq:recall-parameters}), and we deduce
\[\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}\sum_{v\in J_{i+1}^*}\sum_{h=0}^{i-1}p_h\chi_h\cdot \frac{D}{(\log f)^2}\le |J_\ell|\cdot \frac{(r-1)\xi^{r-1}\log f}D\cdot \frac{D}{(\log f)^2}=o(\alpha N).\]
Also, note that $\log p_i=(\sigma i)^{r-1}+\log(\sigma/D^{1/(r-1)})$. Putting all this together, we see that \cref{eq:semi-random-intermediate} is at most
\[\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}\sum_{v\in J_{i+1}^*}\bigg(\log(\sigma/D^{1/(r-1)})+\deg(v)\sum_{h=0}^{i-1}p_{h}\chi_h\bigg)-\alpha N+o(\alpha N).\]
To finish the proof, we observe that
\[
-|J_{\ell}|\log(\sigma/D^{1/(r-1)})-\log(\ell^{|J_{\ell}|})+\alpha N=|J_{\ell}|\log\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac{D^{1/(r-1)}}{\ell\sigma}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)+\alpha N\ge\log\binom{N}{|J_{\ell}|}+o(\alpha N),
\]
again using \cref{eq:recall-parameters}.

body_md:
Recalling \cref{lem:GW-good-events}(3), we have \begin{align*}\mathbb E[\mathbbm{1}_{v\in I_{i+1}\setminus I_{i}}\cdot \mathbbm{1}_\mathcal E]&\le \mathbb P[v\in \Gamma_{i+1}\,|\,v\in A_{i}]\prod_{h=0}^{i-1}\mathbb P[v\in A_{h+1}\,|\,v\in A_{h}\text{ and }\mathcal X_1\cap \dots\cap \mathcal X_{h}\text{ occurs}]\\
&\le p_{i}\prod_{h=0}^{i-1}\frac {q_{h+1}}{q_{h}}\le p_{i}q_{i}=\frac{\sigma}{D^{1/(r-1)}}.\end{align*}
So,
\[\mathbb E[\Lambda(I_1,\dots,I_\ell)\mathbbm{1}_{\mathcal E}]\le\frac{\sigma}{D^{1/(r-1)}}\sum_{v\in \operatorname V(\mathcal G)}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\deg(v)+\frac{D}{(\log f)^2}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}\sum_{h=0}^{i-1}p_h\chi_h\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right).\]
We then note that
\begin{align*}
\frac{\sigma}{D^{1/(r-1)}}\sum^{\ell-1}_{i=0}\sum^{i-1}_{h=0}p_{h}\chi_{h} & =\frac{(r-1)\sigma^{r}}{D^{r/(r-1)}}\sum^{\ell-2}_{h=0}(\ell-1-h)(1+h)^{r-2}\\
 & =(1+o(1))\frac{(r-1)\sigma^{r}}{D^{r/(r-1)}}\int^{\ell}_{0}(\ell-h)h^{r-2}\,dh\\
 & =(1+o(1))\frac{(r-1)\sigma^{r}}{D^{r/(r-1)}}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\frac{\ell^{r}}{r-1}-\frac{\ell^{r}}{r}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)\\
 & =(1+o(1))\frac{1}{r}\cdot\frac{\sigma^{r}\ell^{r}}{D^{r/(r-1)}}=(1+o(1))\frac{1}{r}\alpha^{r}
\end{align*}
and, recalling the definition of $D$,
\[\sum_{v\in \operatorname V(\mathcal G)}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\deg(v)+\frac{D}{(\log f)^2}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)=r|\mathcal G|+ND/(\log f)^2=r|\mathcal G|+o(N\alpha^{1-r}).\]
The desired result follows.

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cref{lem:app-typical-size,lem:app-Y-size,lem:Gamma-approx-I,lem:GW-good-events} we have $\mathbb P[\mathcal E]=1-o(1)$. For $m\in \{1,\dots,N\}$, let $\mathcal E^*_m$ be the event that $|I_\ell|=m$ and $\mathcal E$ occurs. By \cref{claim:app-Lambda}, we can fix $m$ such that $\mathbb P[\mathcal E_m^*]\ge N^{-2}$ and 
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb E[\Lambda(I_1,\dots,I_\ell)\,|\,\mathcal E^*_m]\le \frac{\mathbb E[\Lambda(I_1,\dots,I_\ell) \mathbbm{1}_{\mathcal E}]}{\mathbb P[\mathcal E]-N\cdot N^{-2}}\le \mathcal G(\alpha)+o(\alpha N).\label{eq:Lambda-conditional}
\end{equation}

Now, it suffices to show that the number of possible outcomes of $\vec I=(I_1,\dots,I_\ell)$ satisfying $\mathcal E^*_m$ is at least 
\[\ell^{m}\binom N {m}\exp(-\mathcal G(\alpha)-o(m)).\]

Let $\mathcal J$ be the support of $(I_1,\dots,I_\ell)$ conditional on $\mathcal E_m^*$.
For $\vec J\in \mathcal J$, let \[P(\vec J)=\mathbb P[\vec I=\vec J\text{ and }\mathcal E^*_m\text{ occurs}],\quad P_{\rm{cond}}(\vec J)=\mathbb P[\vec I=\vec J\,|\,\mathcal E^*_m].\] Then
\[|\mathcal J|=\mathbb E[1/P_{\mathrm{cond}}(\vec I)\,|\,\mathcal E^*_m]\ge N^{-2}\mathbb E[1/P(\vec I)\,|\,\mathcal E^*_m]\ge N^{-2}\exp\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big(-\mathbb E[\log P(\vec I)\,|\,\mathcal E^*_m]\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\mathopen{}\mathclose\big).\]
By \cref{claim:app-prob-upper} we have
\[-\mathbb E[\log P(\vec I)\,|\,\mathcal E^*_m]\ge \log\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\ell^{m}\binom{N}{m}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)-\mathbb E[\Lambda(I_1,\dots,I_\ell)\,|\,\mathcal E^*_m]+o(m),\]
and the desired result follows from \cref{eq:Lambda-conditional}.
